target_customer: Electrical engineering teams at aerospace, defense and electronics companies designing circuit boards
problem: Circuit board layout is done largely by hand, with high cost and failure rates, while the engineering talent pool shrinks. JITX generates and optimizes board designs from code.
business_model: B2B software license for a code based PCB design tool, run on customer infrastructure
product_category: Electronic design automation, PCB design software

founders.name: Duncan Haldane
education: UC Berkeley, researched robotics (per Sequoia partnership post)
founders.background_notes: Sequoia says he met Bachrach and Li at UC Berkeley while researching robotics. Degree level not stated.

founders.name: Jonathan Bachrach
founders.background_notes: Per Sequoia, built Chisel, an automated hardware design framework, with Patrick Li.

founders.name: Patrick Li
founders.background_notes: Named as founder by Sequoia but not listed on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a programming language, compiler and automated layout and optimization engine for PCB design is research grade and had to interoperate with entrenched CAD tools.

defensibility.rationale: A specialized language and optimization engine are hard to copy, and designs written in code create lock in, but incumbents own the CAD ecosystem.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The Series A post lists KiCad and Altium as tools JITX integrates with, so JITX positioned alongside incumbents. No acquisition or copying is sourced.

market_need_then: Sequoia (2022) describes manual board layout as a bottleneck with high failure rates and rising PCB demand against a shrinking pool of electrical engineers. No 2018 dated figures found.

branding.domain_note: Uses jitx.com, the exact name as .com; history not found.

brand_strength.rationale: Niche engineering brand with named enterprise customers on its site but no sourced community or brand press.

outcome_analysis: JITX spent roughly four years building a code based PCB design language before announcing a $12 million Series A led by Sequoia on September 2022 with general availability. Its site now lists Honeywell Aerospace, Lockheed Martin and OpenAI as users and partnerships with Siemens, Altium, Ansys and Keysight, and it markets AI driven design. Slow technical build followed by enterprise adoption fits a deep tech tool with no exit yet.
notes: Series A is stated by JITX (blog dated Sept 18, 2022) and Sequoia (byline Sept 20, 2022); the public announcement date was Sept 20, 2022 per other outlets in search results. Neither source mentions earlier funding, and CB Insights shows about $12.1M total, so earlier funding may be negligible but coverage is marked partial. YC lists only Haldane and Bachrach; Patrick Li is named by Sequoia. Competitors: Quilter (founded 2019) and other AI PCB tools are after the batch, and Altium and Cadence evidence is dated 2022 or later, so the list is empty. Outcome search found no acquisition or layoffs.
